Contour: halve per-frame cost, and fix the three safety valves that never fired

The first round cut frequency (24fps -> 8fps), DPR and smoothing passes, but
left the per-frame volume untouched, and all three safety valves turned out to
be dead in the scenario users actually hit.

Measured on real Chromium at 1920x1080 (getImageData flush is the only way to
see the raster cost): 34.7ms -> ~16ms per frame, 60,483 -> 17,913 bezier
segments, build() 66.8ms -> ~35ms.

- CONTOUR_MAX_CELLS 60000 -> 24000. The old cap never engaged at 1080p:
  1920x1080 @ step 6 is exactly 58,101 cells, just under the limit, so the most
  common resolution always got the most expensive grid. The "cost ceiling" was
  decorative.
- Chaikin passes split by animation state (1 animated / 2 static). Two passes
  cost 3.3x the raster of un-smoothed polylines, and at an 8fps slow drift the
  corner detail is unreadable anyway; the static frame still gets the quality.
- contourOnScroll no longer zeroes contourOverBudget. Degrading needs 3
  consecutive over-budget frames, and a reader who scrolls every few hundred ms
  reset that counter every time -- the usage most in need of degradation pinned
  itself to the priciest grid forever. Resume frames now count.
- The learned step survives resize/rebuild, in both the main-thread and worker
  paths. It used to be zeroed, so degradation never outlived a resize, and the
  ladder's last stage deliberately refined back down to the most expensive step.
- Rebuild moved to requestIdleCallback. setTimeout(fn, 0) only deferred the long
  task to the next immediate macrotask; the comment claiming it ran at idle was
  never true. Degraded builds also validate 10 rather than 32 rounds (32 rounds
  at step 12 was a 56ms synchronous block, for the path that exists to be cheap).
- Terrain scratch is reused across attempts instead of reallocating ~3.5MB per
  candidate (up to 112MB of transient garbage per build). Coarse-grid builds
  spiked to 84ms from GC, not computation -- the cost curve was non-monotonic.
  best now stores a salt and is replayed, since the scratch is shared.
- backdrop-filter is gated on contour mode. _frame::before (16px) and
  dialogs/menus (26px, i.e. the settings page you toggle this from) blurred a
  canvas that changes 8x/s, so Chromium had to recompute both 8 times a second
  with zero visual benefit -- the backdrop is a flat colour plus 1px lines.
- Worker cost budget 62.5ms -> 20ms (7.8x the main-thread budget let the raster
  thread burn 500ms/s before degrading). matchMedia is cached instead of
  building 60 MediaQueryLists per second. The 2d context is fetched once.

All 14 suites pass. contour.test.mjs gains 8 regression locks, including
"same engine rebuilt twice is byte-identical" and "two engines do not share
scratch" so the reuse cannot silently break the determinism guarantee.

docs/DESIGN.md records the measurements and the reasoning.

Contour: expose the eight look knobs, and make them apply live

The contour background shipped with one adjustable thing (drift speed); every
other visual parameter was a hard-coded constant. This exposes the ones that
actually change what you see, collected in a folded "Contour advanced" section
that only appears when the background source is contour.

  ink 0-100%      stroke opacity (was hard-coded 55%/70%)
  colour          free picker; empty follows the accent colour
  width           1 / 1.5 / 2 px (was hard-coded lineWidth = 1)
  density         fine/normal/coarse -> cell cap 40000/24000/14000
  levels          12-30, scaled against the 20 baseline
  fps             4 / 8 / 15 (was hard-coded CONTOUR_FPS = 8)
  relief          40-160%, multiplies the gaussian amplitude
  drift           0-200%, multiplies the island breathing offset
  reroll          button: new seed, rebuild, no page refresh

Settings have to be live, so the change-signature guard in
contourApplySwitches had to learn about them. It previously hashed only
"is animating" plus the stroke colour, which meant density / levels / relief /
drift changes produced an identical signature, the function returned early, and
nothing repainted until the page was reloaded -- exactly the "only the
distribution settings need a reload" report. The signature now includes all
five look parameters, and contourApplyLook splits the response: levels, relief,
drift and width only need a re-extract and repaint, while density changes the
grid and must rebuild (debounced 160ms so dragging the slider rebuilds once).

The engine is serialised into the worker with String(fn), so it must never read
`state`. All look parameters travel through setLook() instead, with the
setting-to-constant mapping kept on the main thread in contourLookNow().
The first attempt called contourLineWidth() straight from drawTo and the worker
died with a ReferenceError, silently falling back to the main thread.

Also fixes a real bug found while writing the tests: with drift at 0 the
terrain kept moving, because the base sine's phase term did not take the drift
factor. Both terms now do, so 0 is genuinely static.

Contour labels are opt-in and default off. Measured on real Chromium at
1080p / 21 levels / 86 paths, drawing them costs +141% per frame (draw 2.8 ->
6.5ms, 76 fillText calls), so they are limited to the static speed setting,
where only one frame is ever drawn. Labelling each level once instead of each
path, and probing several points along the path to avoid the canvas edges,
brings it to +32% (3.7ms, 21 calls). At any animated speed the labels are
suppressed outright rather than costing the raster thread every frame.

All 14 suites pass, including 21 new regression locks: the eight settings must
reach the engine, the look signature must contain all five distribution keys,
a rebuilt engine must still be byte-identical, and two engines must not share
scratch. docs/DESIGN.md records the measurements and the worker constraint.

feat: rework background ground, reorganize settings, add screenshots

Background ground is now a small compositor with three modes:
- glow: 2-6 light sources, each with its own colour, strength and X/Y
- bands: 2-6 strips, each its own colour, cut angle 0-360 degrees
- blend: both

Density ceiling raised to 100%. Gradient mode no longer applies the
wallpaper veil, blur, saturation or upscale — those were designed for
photo wallpapers and were eating most of the glow.

Settings page reorganized from 11 groups down to 5:
- all colour controls collected into a single "Colour" group
- Glass group keeps only 2 permanent rows (switch + background source);
  the rest folds into "Common settings" and "Current background only",
  the latter rendering just the parameters for the selected source
- removed settings that did nothing meaningful: apply-scope, background
  variant, accent presets, prose brightness, and all three preview blocks

Fixed a regression where the wallpaper local-path input and the fit
dropdown had been dropped during earlier edits.

Adds screenshots for the gradient ground and the contour background.

chore: prepare v1.1.0 release

- bump version 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0
- add CHANGELOG.md covering the background-ground rework, settings
  reorganization, removals and fixes
- document how to pin a release in both README languages

fix: glass the transient popovers that have no role attribute

The file-change diff popover and the conversation-history popover are
position:fixed elements with no role, so the [role="dialog"] and
[role="menu"] rules never matched them. The only code that touched them
lived behind the "Solid floats" switch (off by default), and it pinned
them fully opaque instead of glassing them — so by default they rendered
as flat boxes over live text.

They now follow the glass in two layers:
- default: same delta-alpha compositing and blur as dialogs/menus, with a
  slightly higher +0.03 readability compensation since these are
  transient and read immediately
- "Solid floats" on: still pins them opaque; its rule wins by source order

The HoverCard bubble had the same problem in a different shape — its
background is the hard-coded --dsw-hovercard-bg, unreachable by any token
override. It is now overridden at the variable itself with a translucent
glass value, resolved through runtime class detection.

Bumps version to 1.1.1.

fix: blur the turn-preview popover (two stacked problems)

The popover is TurnNavigator's turn preview, class `xpvNua_preview`.
v1.1.1 injected the right rule but it never applied, for two
independent reasons:

1. Class name format. The rule matched [class*="_preview_"], which only
   covers CSS Modules hashed names. This popover's class is
   `xpvNua_preview` — module name then element name, no leading
   underscore — so the selector never matched. Now uses
   [class*="preview"], excluding the plugin's own dmt- classes.

2. contain: layout blocked the backdrop sampling. Its parent nav has
   contain: layout, which establishes a new containing block and
   confines backdrop-filter sampling to that box — and the box is only
   28px wide, so the blur had nothing to sample. A new rule clears
   contain on any ancestor that directly contains a popover, via
   :has(). The hashed class name cannot be hard-coded since it changes
   every build; if :has() is unsupported the rule is ignored and the
   popover degrades to "translucent but not frosted", as before.

Adds preview-contain-test.html, the side-by-side page used to isolate
the contain behaviour, and the two console tools used for diagnosis.

Bumps version to 1.1.2.

fix: detect popovers at runtime instead of matching class substrings

v1.1.2 widened the popover selector to [class*="preview"] to cover both
class naming formats. But the host has eight class names containing
"preview" and only two are popovers — the rest are JSON-tree syntax
colouring, which live inside diff regions and only declare `color`.
Painting them as surfaces put a dark box under every JSON value, so diff
regions went solid.

The substring selector is gone. detectPopoverClasses() now scans the
stylesheets and accepts a class only if both conditions hold:

- the name matches a popover naming pattern (either `_preview_<hash>_<n>`
  or `<hash>_preview`)
- the rule declares a background

A popover has to paint its own surface; an inner text block does not.
That criterion follows the host implementation rather than a class-name
list, so a new previewXxx class in a future host build cannot silently
break it again.

Generated rules now target exact class names, and the contain override
uses the same detected names.

Also fixes the format-A regex: it was missing the leading underscore, so
`._preview_38jqx_52` never matched and only the format-B names were
detected.

Bumps version to 1.1.3.

fix: pass detected popover classes to buildGlassSheet

buildGlassSheet gained a sixth parameter for the detected popover class
names, but the real call site never passed it. The edit landed on an
identically-worded string in the module's export block instead of on the
function that builds the stylesheet. The rule-generation logic was
correct and its unit tests passed — the rule simply never received any
class names at runtime, so it was never emitted.

- all call sites now pass the parameter
- a test asserts every runtime call site includes it (mutation-tested by
  removing the argument, which turns the assertion red)
- detection also runs inside syncGlassSheet, not only syncCardSheet:
  syncCardSheet runs early in startup when the host may not have
  injected all stylesheets yet, and there was no second attempt. Bounded
  at 60 retries, after which the result is cached.
- the status object now exposes `popovers` (count of detected classes) so
  this class of failure is visible instead of silent

Bumps version to 1.1.4.

fix: stop stacking the frosted haze on nested surfaces

Code blocks looked noticeably whiter and duller than other glass
surfaces. The haze is a translucent white gradient on the shared
glassSurface constant, which every glass surface used — including
nested ones. A code block sits inside a card or column, so the haze
stacked: 1 - (1-0.08)^2 = 15.4%, nearly double the configured value.

Split by nesting level:
- glassSurface      (haze)    outermost: columns, cards, dialogs,
                              popovers, composer
- glassSurfaceFlat  (no haze) nested: code blocks, pre, inline code

Both keep box-shadow and border; those draw on the element's own edges
and do not accumulate brightness.

Lowering the global haze value would have been the wrong fix — it exists
to give the outermost layer its material feel, and thinning it everywhere
would flatten single-layer surfaces.

Bumps version to 1.1.5.

fix: give nested surfaces a third of the haze, not zero

v1.1.5 removed the haze from nested surfaces to stop it stacking — but
removing it is not the same as reducing it. Code blocks lost their frost
entirely.

The haze is a white overlay, so two layers combine as 1-(1-a)(1-b):

  8% + 8%  = 15.4%  too heavy (the original bug)
  8% + 0%  =  8%    child does not whiten at all — haze is gone
  8% + 2.7%= 10.2%  matches the surrounding surfaces

Zero does not work because a code block paints its own fairly opaque
surface, which covers the parent's haze. Without a layer of its own, that
surface genuinely has no haze.

Nested surfaces now get haze/3. A third rather than half because a code
block's own fill is one tier more opaque than a card's, so the haze
carries less visual weight on it — full value reads too white, zero
reads as absent.

Bumps version to 1.1.6.

fix: nested haze a eighth, not a third

v1.1.6 gave code blocks haze/3, which combined to 10.5% — visibly denser
than the 8% single-layer baseline. Now haze/8, combining to 8.9%, which
matches the surrounding surfaces.

  divisor 1  -> child 8.00%  combined 15.36%  two full layers (original bug)
  divisor 3  -> child 2.67%  combined 10.45%  v1.1.6, still too dense
  divisor 8  -> child 1.00%  combined  8.92%  matches baseline

The earlier two attempts each had an unclear target: v1.1.5 optimised for
"don't stack too thick" and landed on zero, leaving that surface with no
haze at all; v1.1.6 optimised for "the haze should be visible" and
overshot. The right target is combined density close to the single-layer
baseline — the child only needs enough to avoid reading as absent.

The test now bounds it from both sides: 0.005 <= haze < 0.02. Below the
lower bound it is invisible; above the upper bound the combined value
exceeds 9.8% and reads denser than everything else. All three wrong
versions (zero, a third, full) are caught by mutation testing.

Bumps version to 1.1.7.

feat: background brightness for wallpaper mode

It was gradient-only before. The two sources need different
implementations but share one meaning:

  gradient   -> mixTowards() shifts the generated base colour
                0 = pure black, 100 = pure white (deliberate; the
                ambience layer fades with it)
  wallpaper  -> CSS brightness(), on the same filter chain as blur and
                saturate; 50 = 1.0, 0 = full black, 100 = doubles

Wallpaper stops at doubling rather than pure white — pure white would
erase the photo's detail, whereas gradient reaching pure white is
intentional.

Contour mode is unaffected: its line colour comes straight from the
accent colour, so brightness would only distort it, same reasoning as
saturate.

The settings row is now shared by both sources instead of being gated on
gradient alone.

Bumps version to 1.1.8.

fix: match card bodies by whole class token, not substring

The card glass rule matched [class*="flL80G_file"] — a substring match.
CSS Modules give every inner element of the same component a shared
prefix (flL80G_fileBody / fileName / fileIcon; KuQXFq_cardTitle / cardOpen
/ cards), so the haze, border and shadow landed on each of those rows
too — the "boxes inside boxes" the user screenshotted on the deliverable
and plan cards.

Switched the six card prefixes to [class~="..."] (whole-word class
match). bubble deliberately keeps *=: message bubbles carry per-package
hashes in their token (cJsG2q_bubble / v1fjQa_bubble) that must not be
hard-coded, and no bubbleXxx inner elements exist in the host.

Third instance of the same mistake class as the v1.1.7 popover selector:
substring matching is unsafe against CSS Modules naming because inner
elements share the owner's prefix. Wherever the exact token is known,
use ~=.

13 new assertions; mutation (reverting to *=) turns all 13 red.

Bumps version to 1.1.9.

感谢提交！已检查 `dsh-skills-panel@1.0.3`。补丁和入口完整，但发布包的 `lib/client.js` 内嵌了作者机器上的 10 项技能及绝对路径，Host 入口没有读取当前用户技能的逻辑；安装后默认显示的并不是安装者自己的技能。

请先清理发布包中的个人技能清单和绝对路径，并提供适用于当前用户环境的初始化/刷新方式，或从当前 DSH 实例读取技能。现有 `scripts/sync-skills.mjs` 中写死的 `D:/tools/...` 路径也请改为可发现或可配置，并说明在哪里运行、技能变化后如何刷新。发布修正版后在这里留言，我们再复核。🙂
